name: MyAlgo
rootCause: Algorand ecological wallet MyAlgo issued a reminder on Twitter that the hack occurred more than a week ago, and no other actions have taken place since then. The attacked users all had large amounts of funds on their accounts and used mnemonic wallets with keys stored in the browser. ZachXBT, an on-chain data analyst, tweeted: “Due to the attack on MyAlgo, Algorand’s ecological wallet, from February 19th to 21st, more than $9.2 million in assets (19.5 million ALGOs, 3.5 million USDCs, etc.) may have been stolen on Algorand. ChangeNow shared that they were able to freeze $1.5 million.”

descriptions.text: Algorand ecological wallet MyAlgo issued a reminder on Twitter that the hack occurred more than a week ago, and no other actions have taken place since then. The attacked users all had large amounts of funds on their accounts and used mnemonic wallets with keys stored in the browser. ZachXBT, an on-chain data analyst, tweeted: “Due to the attack on MyAlgo, Algorand’s ecological wallet, from February 19th to 21st, more than $9.2 million in assets (19.5 million ALGOs, 3.5 million USDCs, etc.) may have been stolen on Algorand. ChangeNow shared that they were able to freeze $1.5 million.”

Between January and March 2023, MyAlgo’s Algorand browser wallet was compromised through a supply‑chain attack on its content delivery network, enabling silent exfiltration of private keys and draining over $9.2m from affected user accounts. A malicious JavaScript worker was injected into the CDN serving the MyAlgo web wallet, enabling attackers to steal mnemonic phrases and private keys from users who unlocked their wallets, resulting in direct wallet drains. The exact method by which the CDN API key was obtained remains uncertain.
